judgment.rationale: Both are Indicator-grain statements at the same resolved coordinate (BASIC 4, rank 0) in Strand 2: Algebra, Sub-strand 1: Patterns and Relationships. B4.2.1.1.1 requires learners to 'Describe the pattern found in a given table or chart' (under Content Standard B4.2.1.1 on identifying/describing patterns in tables and charts), while B4.2.1.2.1 requires them to 'Create a concrete representation of a given pattern displayed in a table or chart' (under Content Standard B4.2.1.2 on translating among representations of a pattern). Shared LC tags ('chart','pattern','table') plus the added 'concrete representation' tag show extension into a new representational mode rather than mere repetition. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), but the retained statement text, codes, and hierarchy are sufficient and consistent.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (same coordinate rank 1) under Strand 4: Data, Sub-Strand 1 'Data Collection, Organisation, Presentation, Interpretation and Analysis', but sit under different Content Standards: B5.4.1.1 (differentiate first-hand vs second-hand data) and B5.4.1.2 (construct and interpret double bar graphs). The first indicator has learners locate examples of second-hand data in print/electronic media (LC tags: data collection, media, second-hand data); the second has learners draw and use double bar graphs with title, labelled axes and legend for up to 3 paired categories (LC tags: data representation, double bar graph, solve problems). They are complementary stages of the same data-handling cycle — sourcing/recognising data and representing/interpreting it — giving substantive conceptual coherence, but the bounded evidence shows no statement-level dependency: graphing double bar graphs is not stated to require identifying second-hand media sources, and the two are same-rank peers, so no developmental direction is substantiated. Textual/LC overlap is limited to the generic token 'data' (Jaccard ~0.05–0.08), and code-prefix/page proximity are weak signals only, so relatesTo rather than buildsTowards.

They share genuine algebraic problem-solving coherence — using an identified rule/relationship to resolve an unknown quantity — so the pattern-rule work and equation-based work meaningfully reinforce each other. However, neither statement's content presupposes the other: equation representation of an unknown does not depend on extending sequences by a pattern rule, and vice versa; the shared tokens are limited to generic 'solve a problem' wording (LC tag Jaccard 0.07), and same-rank placement offers no substantive developmental ordering evidence. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment rather than a direction. judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (same statement-type grain, same coordinate rank 1) under the same Content Standard 'Demonstrate an understanding of volume of common 3D shapes' in Strand 3 Geometry and Measurement / Sub-Strand Measurement. The second SFI (B5.3.3.2.2) establishes the foundational measuring skill: quantifying the volume of a box by counting how many 1cm³ cubes it contains. The first SFI (B5.3.2.2.3) applies and extends that skill to a comparative/constructive task: generating multiple differently shaped boxes that hold the same volume, which presupposes being able to determine a box's volume in unit cubes and hold that quantity invariant across different dimensions (the source context for the first cites an exemplar 'Given 12 centimetre...' cubes). This is a substantive same-rank developmental step from measuring volume to conserving/reorganising volume, so proficiency in the second supports success in the first. Direction is grounded in the statement content, not in code prefixes or page order; note the codes 'B5.3.2.2.3' and 'B5.3.3.2.2' are inconsistent with the shared parent code B5.3.2.2, and the parent carries a same_code_different_content audit flag, so code evidence was not used as positive hierarchy evidence. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), so full exemplar detail is unavailable.

producer_judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (same rank 1, same grain) under Strand 3 Geometry and Measurement, but in different Sub-Strands: B5.3.1.1.2 sits under 'Lines and Shapes' (paper folding with cut-out squares and rectangles to investigate sides, angles and diagonals properties, LCs on properties of sides/angles/diagonals) while B5.3.3.3.2 sits under 'Measurement - Angles' (measure given angles with a protractor and classify as right, acute, obtuse, reflex). They share substantive conceptual coherence about angles: informal hands-on investigation of the angle properties of quadrilaterals complements formal angle measurement and classification. However, neither statement presupposes the other — the folding task investigates shape attributes without requiring protractor measurement, and the measurement/classification indicator is framed generically for given angles — so no developmental dependency is evidenced, and same-rank direction lacks the required substantive support. Evidence is bounded: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), which limits detection of any explicit sequencing.
